content.user_title: Clarify User Decisions With Focused Questions
content.value_statement: AI agents can waste time when requirements or preferences are unclear. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a practical pattern for asking focused questions.
actual_capabilities: Defines when an agent should ask the user instead of deciding alone.
Shows how to present clear options with short trade-off descriptions.
Encourages agents to explain why each question matters.
Recommends batching related questions to reduce interruptions.
Covers clarification, confirmation, decision, and scope questions.
limitations: It provides interaction guidance, not an automated decision engine.
It depends on the host agent supporting user question tools.
It does not validate answers or enforce workflow state.
It does not cover complex survey design or research interviews.

use_cases.title: Clarify Product Requirements
use_cases.description: Ask targeted questions when feature scope, priority, or acceptance criteria are unclear.

use_cases.title: Choose Technical Direction
use_cases.description: Present implementation options with trade-offs before choosing an architecture or integration path.

use_cases.title: Confirm Task Scope
use_cases.description: Check assumptions before starting work that could expand beyond the original request.

prompt_templates.title: Ask One Clarifying Question
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with one missing detail.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the ask-user skill to ask one specific clarification question before you proceed.

prompt_templates.title: Offer Two Options
prompt_templates.scenario: A decision has two practical paths.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the ask-user skill to present two options, explain the trade-offs, and ask which path to take.

prompt_templates.title: Batch Related Decisions
prompt_templates.scenario: Several related choices block the next step.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the ask-user skill to batch related questions, keep each option concise, and explain why the answers matter.

prompt_templates.title: Decide Whether To Ask
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the ask-user skill to identify which choices need user input and which choices you can decide independently.

output_examples.input: The user asks for authentication but does not choose a method.
output_examples.output: The agent asks whether to use JWT or sessions, gives concise trade-offs, and waits for the user's choice.

output_examples.input: A task includes unclear performance requirements.
output_examples.output: The agent asks whether fast means a specific response time target or simply faster than the current behavior.

output_examples.input: Several related settings affect one implementation plan.
output_examples.output: The agent groups the questions together so the user can answer once before work begins.

best_practices: Ask specific questions tied to a real decision.
Provide a recommendation when trade-offs are clear.
Batch related questions when several answers are needed.
anti_patterns: Do not ask broad questions without context.
Do not interrupt the user for low-impact choices.
Do not hide important trade-offs from the options.

faq.question: What does this skill help an agent do?
faq.answer: It helps an agent ask clear user questions when requirements, scope, or preferences are unclear.

faq.question: Does this skill make decisions automatically?
faq.answer: No. It explains when to ask the user and when a low-risk decision can be made directly.

faq.question: Can this work in Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: When should the agent ask the user?
faq.answer: The agent should ask when preferences matter, scope is unclear, or multiple valid approaches have trade-offs.

faq.question: When should the agent decide without asking?
faq.answer: The agent can decide when a best practice exists, the choice is low impact, or the change is reversible.

faq.question: Does the skill require network access?
faq.answer: No. The skill is documentation for user interaction patterns and does not require network access.
